description: Evaluates the 'Before You Start (Agent Bootstrap)', 'Converting a Slurm Workload' and 'Investigating a Managed Job' section behavior

evals.name: happy-path-server-running
evals.prompt: I want to launch an 8xH100 cluster for training a LLaMA model. My SkyPilot is already set up.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs `sky api status -l 1`, sees the server is running (table output with request data), skips rest of bootstrap (no `sky check`, no install, no `sky api start`), and proceeds directly to help write the task YAML or run `sky launch`.

assertions.text: Agent runs `sky api status` (or `sky api status -l 1`) as the first SkyPilot command
Agent does NOT run `sky check` when the server is already running
Agent does NOT run `sky api start` or `sky api login` when the server is already running
Agent proceeds to help with the user's actual task (launching H100 cluster) without unnecessary bootstrap steps

evals.name: server-not-running-local-setup
evals.prompt: I just installed SkyPilot and want to try launching a GPU instance on AWS. I don't have a remote API server.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs `sky api status -l 1`, detects 'SkyPilot API server is not running.', asks about local vs remote, user indicates local, agent runs `sky api start`, re-checks with `sky api status -l 1`, then runs `sky check` for credentials since this is a fresh setup.

assertions.text: Agent runs `sky api status` as the first SkyPilot command
Agent asks the user whether they have a remote server or want to start locally
Agent runs `sky api start` after user confirms local setup
Agent re-runs `sky api status` after starting the server to confirm it's reachable
Agent runs `sky check` since this is a fresh setup

evals.name: server-not-running-remote-connect
evals.prompt: I need to connect to our team's SkyPilot API server at https://skypilot.internal.company.com and launch a fine-tuning job.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs `sky api status -l 1`, detects server not running, recognizes user already provided a remote URL, runs `sky api login -e https://skypilot.internal.company.com` without asking unnecessary questions, re-checks status, then proceeds to help with the fine-tuning job.

assertions.text: Agent runs `sky api status` as the first SkyPilot command
Agent uses `sky api login -e https://skypilot.internal.company.com` (not `sky api start`) since the user provided a remote endpoint
Agent does NOT ask the user for the server URL again since they already provided it
Agent re-runs `sky api status` after connecting to confirm it's reachable

evals.name: slurm-sbatch-time-not-autostop
evals.prompt:
Convert this to SkyPilot for our Slurm cluster:
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --nodes=2
#SBATCH --gpus-per-node=8
#SBATCH --time=24:00:00
#SBATCH --account=ai-research
srun python train.py
evals.expected_output: Agent produces a task YAML with num_nodes: 2, resources.accelerators: H100:8 (or asks for the GRES name), and puts both --time and --account under config.slurm.sbatch_options. The bare `srun` is dropped because `run` already executes on every node. Agent recommends `sky jobs launch` for this batch script.

assertions.text: Agent maps --time to config.slurm.sbatch_options.time
Agent does NOT map --time to autostop, which is unsupported on Slurm
Agent maps --account to config.slurm.sbatch_options.account
Agent puts num_nodes at task level, not under resources
Agent does NOT wrap the run command in `srun` again
Agent recommends `sky jobs launch` (not `sky launch`) for this batch script

evals.name: slurm-job-array-to-num-jobs
evals.prompt: On Slurm I run `sbatch --array=0-99 shard.sh` and the script reads $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID to pick its shard. What's the SkyPilot equivalent?
evals.expected_output: Agent answers `sky jobs launch --num-jobs 100` and maps $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID to $SKYPILOT_JOB_RANK (with $SKYPILOT_NUM_JOBS for the count). May also mention pools for reusing workers across submissions.

assertions.text: Agent uses `sky jobs launch --num-jobs 100`
Agent maps $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID to $SKYPILOT_JOB_RANK
Agent does NOT propose a shell for-loop as the primary answer

evals.name: why-is-my-managed-job-pending
evals.prompt: My managed job 42 has been PENDING for 20 minutes on our Slurm cluster. Why? SkyPilot is already set up.
evals.expected_output: Agent reads `details` from `sky jobs queue -v -o json` and finds the Slurm pending reason with its partition (e.g. `Launching (pending: QOSGrpGRES; partition: h200)`), explains that category (quota vs no free capacity vs dependency vs held) and what to do about it. Does not claim the job is stuck in SkyPilot's own queue when the reason is Slurm's.

assertions.text: Agent runs `sky jobs queue -v -o json` (`-v` is required for the `details` field) and reads the job's details
Agent reads the Slurm pending reason and its partition from `details`
Agent explains the pending reason in plain terms (quota, capacity, dependency, or held) with a next step
Agent does NOT poll with `sleep` + `sky jobs queue`
Agent does NOT tear down the jobs controller as a first step

evals.name: what-happened-to-my-job
evals.prompt: Managed job 17 keeps flipping between RUNNING and RECOVERING. Show me what happened.
evals.expected_output: Agent reads `sky jobs queue -v -o json` for `details` / `failure_reason` / `recovery_count`, then pulls `sky jobs logs 17 --controller --no-follow` for the recovery history, and points out that a repeated identical reason means a persistent cause the controller cannot fix by retrying.

assertions.text: Agent reads `details`, `failure_reason` and `recovery_count` from `sky jobs queue -v -o json`
Agent identifies the recurring RECOVERING reason from the events
Agent uses `--tail` or `--no-follow` when fetching logs rather than streaming the full log
